void_v0.doc: Entry pause (blocks `wrap`). The ONLY pause in this contract.\nThere is deliberately no exit pause - see the file-level comment.
void_v0.name: Paused

tuple_v0.doc:
Set on admit by `allow` and `add_venue`; REMOVED on `disallow`.
There is no function in this contract that writes `false` to an
`Allowed` key - the entry is either present (`allow`-side) or
absent (`disallow`-side), matching the unfreeze pattern. Venue
addresses are structurally protected from `disallow` (see the
file-level comment and `#16 VenueProtected`), so the venue
subset of this map remains monotone-additive; non-venue
admittees can be removed by admin and re-admitted.
tuple_v0.name: Allowed

tuple_v0.doc:
Sender-side freeze. Set on `freeze`, REMOVED on `unfreeze` (not
written as `false`). A missing entry means NOT frozen; a present
entry means frozen. The remove-on-unfreeze pattern keeps the
invariant symmetric with the age-out failure mode: an archived
Frozen entry fails at footprint load, which fails CLOSED.
tuple_v0.name: Frozen

tuple_v0.doc:
Venue marker. Set on `add_venue`, NEVER unset (no remove_venue
function exists). Presence is the semantic; readers use `has()`,
never read the stored value. A marked address is one the operator
has declared part of the venue payout path (Blend pool, facade,
etc.) and `freeze` must refuse to point at it because freezing
the venue sender would strand every supplied balance until
unfrozen - see `add_venue` and the file-level comment.
tuple_v0.name: Venue

function_v0.doc: Pull the restricted asset in, mint wrapped 1:1. The `from` is\ngated: a non-allowlisted address cannot wrap because that would\nbe a way to acquire the wrapped token.
function_v0.name: wrap

function_v0.doc:
Admin adds an address to the transfer allowlist. The counterpart
is `disallow`, which REMOVES the entry rather than writing `false`
(presence is the semantic, matching the unfreeze pattern).
`disallow` is REFUSED against any address the operator has marked
with `add_venue` (panics with `#16 VenueProtected`); the venue
guard is mandatory because removing the Blend pool or the facade
from the allowlist strands every supplier at once. The new entry
is bumped to the network maximum TTL because admission is
permanent-by-design (a quiet-but-readmitted member must never see
their entry archive) and re-`allow` after `disallow` re-applies
the same bump.
function_v0.name: allow

function_v0.doc:

then refuses that address with `#8`. `wrap` and `unwrap` are
NOT affected - a frozen member can still be paid out by a
venue (Blend payout is `transfer(pool -> member)` where `from`
is the pool, not the member) and can still redeem their own
wrapped balance. Admins can be frozen; the admin multisig
itself is the only address that can write the entry. Bumps
the entry to the network maximum TTL because an archived
Frozen entry fails at footprint load, which fails CLOSED.

any `from` - and Blend's payout is `transfer(pool -> member)`
where the POOL is the sender. The guard closes that. There is

function_v0.doc:
Burn wrapped, return the restricted asset. Deliberately has NO
eligibility check on `from`: the underlying asset's authorization
flags refuse the payout if the holder is no longer eligible
(`SAC` error `#11`). Adding a check here would be redundant and
risks diverging from the asset's own view. Exit is structurally
unpausable - see the file-level comment.

counterpart of `allow`. REMOVES the storage entry rather than
writing `false` - mirrors `unfreeze` exactly so the invariant is

function_v0.doc:
Gate on the RECIPIENT (`to`). This is `pool/src/pool/submit.rs:243`
(`transfer(pool, to, amount)`) plus the pool-initiated credit
paths; an ineligible `to` is refused with `#1`. Gate is a pure
local storage read - see the file-level comment.

Sender-side freeze: a frozen `from` is refused with `#8`. The
check is on `from` ONLY - deliberately NOT on `to` (a frozen
address can still RECEIVE wrapped tokens, which is what makes
a venue payout into a frozen member succeed). See the
file-level comment for why this is the only place the check
lives and why that placement is the only acceptable one.
function_v0.name: transfer

function_v0.doc:
Admin reverses a freeze. REMOVES the storage entry rather than
writing `false`. Only frozen addresses then hold a Frozen
entry; an archived entry fails at footprint load, which fails
CLOSED (transfer blocked). The remove-on-unfreeze pattern
keeps the invariant symmetric with the age-out failure mode -
missing = not frozen, present = frozen. See the file-level
comment for why this gate and the allowlist stay separate:
`unfreeze` reverses a SENDER-side restriction and `allow`
reverses a RECIPIENT-side one, so neither substitutes for the
other.
function_v0.name: unfreeze

function_v0.doc:
Admin marks an address as a venue AND allowlists it in a single
call. ADD-ONLY - there is deliberately NO `remove_venue` function:
if venue status could be removed, an admin could strip the marker
from a venue and then call `freeze` on it, which would defeat the
`freeze` guard and re-open the strand-every-supplier failure mode
this contract is built to refuse. The marker is monotone-additive
and, since `disallow` exists, it is now the ONLY monotone record
here: the allowlist is revocable for ordinary admittees, while
this marker must stay one-way because both guards it backs
(`#9` on `freeze`, `#16` on `disallow`) are one-way trips.

Marking and allowlisting happen together because a venue that is
not on the allowlist cannot receive wrapped tokens at all
(`transfer` rejects with `#1`), so splitting them across two
calls would leave a window in which the two records disagree.

function_v0.doc:
Constructor. Runs ATOMICALLY as part of contract creation, which
is the only window in which admin / underlying / name / symbol
can be set. There is no separate `init` step and so no init
front-run window for an attacker to claim admin: the only way
admin is set is the deploy transaction itself. Requires
`--admin <A> --underlying <U> --name <N> --symbol <S>` at
deploy time.

function_v0.doc:
Like `unwrap`, but with a caller-chosen upper bound on `amount`
that the contract binds the auth to. Sibling of `unwrap`; the
existing `unwrap` is unchanged.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The `unwrap` auth is `require_auth()`, which
infers the signed args from the invocation. For a facade that
computes `amount` from live pool state AFTER calling the pool
(e.g. an overpaid Repay where the residue is the pool refund),
the actual `amount` argument can drift between simulation and
inclusion (~17 stroops/second of accruing interest on this
debt) and the signed auth no longer matches the invocation
- the transaction fails with `Error(auth, invalid_action)` on
the `unwrap` sub-invocation. `require_auth_for_args` lets the
CONTRACT decide which values belong to the auth, so we authorise
over `cap` only (a stable value the facade knows from the
member's own request vector before any sub-invocation) and
allow `amount` to drift without invalidating the tree.
